💛 ANAK NAKAL ATAU SEDANG KESULITAN MENGATUR EMOSI?

Pernah merasa Si Kecil tiba-tiba menangis, marah, atau sulit ditenangkan?

Sebelum buru-buru melabeli anak sebagai nakal, yuk, coba pahami apa yang sebenarnya sedang ia rasakan.

Karena tidak semua perilaku yang terlihat sulit dihadapi merupakan bentuk kenakalan. Bisa jadi, anak sedang mengalami kesulitan dalam mengenali, mengungkapkan, dan mengatur emosinya.

🌱 Apa yang perlu kita pahami?

✨ Anak yang melanggar aturan mungkin membutuhkan arahan dan pemahaman tentang batasan.

✨ Anak yang belum mampu meregulasi emosi mungkin membutuhkan bantuan untuk menenangkan diri, memahami perasaannya, dan belajar merespons situasi dengan lebih baik.

Lalu, apa yang bisa dilakukan orang tua?

❤️ Dampingi anak saat emosinya belum stabil. ❤️ Bantu anak mengenali dan menyebutkan perasaannya. ❤️ Berikan batasan dengan cara yang tenang dan konsisten. ❤️ Ajarkan cara mengelola emosi secara bertahap.

Ingat, anak tidak selalu membutuhkan teguran. Terkadang, mereka lebih membutuhkan kehadiran, pemahaman, dan pendampingan kita.

Karena di balik perilaku yang menantang, ada keterampilan yang masih perlu dipelajari dan dikembangkan.

Yuk, menjadi orang tua yang bukan hanya melihat perilaku anak, tetapi juga memahami kebutuhan di baliknya. 💕

“Kakak, mengalah ya… kamu kan sudah besar.”

Kalimat sederhana yang sering kita ucapkan kepada anak pertama. Tapi pernahkah kita berpikir, bahwa kakak juga masih anak-anak yang ingin dibela, didengar, dan dimengerti?

Saat adik menangis, kakak diminta mengalah.
Saat kakak marah, kakak dianggap harus lebih sabar.
Padahal, mereka sama-sama sedang belajar mengelola emosi.

Menjadi orang tua bukan tentang menentukan siapa yang salah dan siapa yang harus mengalah. Tetapi tentang mengajarkan bahwa setiap perasaan berharga, setiap anak berhak didengar, dan setiap masalah bisa diselesaikan dengan adil.

Jangan sampai kita terlalu sibuk meminta kakak menjadi dewasa, sampai lupa bahwa ia juga masih membutuhkan pelukan dan perlindungan.

Yuk, mulai belajar memperlakukan kakak dan adik dengan adil, bukan selalu sama, tetapi sesuai kebutuhan dan perasaan masing-masing.

SENTUHAN SEKECIL INI BISA MEMICU REFLEKS ALAMI KAKI BAYI?

Coba ketuk pelan telapak kaki bayi mengikuti irama lagu, perhatikan jari-jari kakinya menekuk sendiri. Ini bukan kebetulan, Yah. 

Gerakan ini disebut plantar grasp reflex, salah satu refleks primitif bawaan yang sudah ada sejak bayi masih di dalam kandungan. Menurut Cleveland Clinic dalam artikel Newborn Reflexes, refleks ini muncul saat telapak kaki bayi disentuh, menyebabkan jari-jari kakinya menekuk secara otomatis tanpa bisa dikendalikan bayi. Refleks bawaan seperti ini menjadi salah satu tanda bahwa sistem saraf bayi berkembang dengan baik pada tahun pertama kehidupannya.

Artinya, permainan sederhana ini bukan sekadar lucu-lucuan. Ayah sedang mengamati salah satu tonggak perkembangan alami bayi sambil menciptakan momen bonding lewat sentuhan dan nyanyian.

Cara melakukannya:

Posisikan bayi telentang, dalam kondisi tenang dan tidak lapar.
Pegang kedua kaki bayi dengan lembut.
Ketuk pelan telapak kakinya mengikuti irama lagu yang Ayah nyanyikan.
Ucapkan, “Tuk tuk tuk... kaki Adik ikut lagu Ayah ya!”
Perhatikan jari kakinya menekuk sebagai respons alami.
Penting: Gunakan sentuhan yang sangat ringan. Telapak kaki bayi usia ini sangat sensitif. Hentikan segera bila bayi menarik kakinya, menangis, atau tampak tidak nyaman.

Aktivitas ini bersifat permainan sensorik ringan, bukan pemeriksaan medis. Refleks bawaan umumnya berangsur menghilang seiring pertumbuhan bayi. Jika ada kekhawatiran terhadap perkembangan bayi, konsultasikan dengan dokter anak.

Bantu anak memahami emosinya ✅ 
❌ Jangan buru-buru bertanya: “Kamu kenapa?”

Kalau ingin membantu anak memahami dan menamai emosinya, AyBun bisa coba:

🤍 1. Bantu beri nama emosinya
“Kayaknya kamu kecewa ya, karena tadi nggak boleh main.”

🤍 2. Perhatikan tanda-tanda kecil
Ekspresi wajah, nada bicara, gerakan tubuh, sampai perubahan perilakunya.

🤍 3. Tanyakan sensasi di tubuhnya
“Perut kamu terasa nggak enak waktu tadi takut?”

🤍 4. Gunakan cerita & permainan
Boneka, buku cerita, atau bermain peran bisa membantu anak mengenal berbagai emosi.

🤍 5. Ceritakan emosi kita juga
“Bunda tadi sempat kesal karena pekerjaan Bunda belum selesai.”
Anak belajar dari contoh.

🤍 6. Jangan menghakimi emosinya
Hindari “Jangan cengeng”, “Gitu aja nangis”, atau “Kamu kan anak besar.”

🤍 7. Jangan terlalu fokus pada perilakunya
Tantrum, marah, atau menangis sering kali hanya “puncak gunung es”. Coba lihat perasaan yang ada di balik perilaku tersebut.

Dan yang nggak kalah penting: nggak harus terus-terusan bertanya sampai anak mau cerita.

Kadang cukup bantu anak mengenali emosinya, lalu beri ruang.

Sampai akhirnya anak belajar sendiri:
“Oh, ternyata aku sedang kecewa.”
“Ternyata aku marah karena merasa nggak didengarkan.”

Karena tujuan akhirnya bukan anak selalu bisa menjawab pertanyaan kita, tapi anak mampu mengenali dan memahami perasaannya sendiri.

Sering kali, yang paling diingat anak bukan seberapa cepat kita menyelesaikan masalahnya, tetapi bagaimana cara kita merespons perasaannya.

🤍 Kalau akhir-akhir ini si Kecil maunya nempel terus, menyusu lebih sering, dan jadi gampang rewel… tenang dulu ya, Mommy.

Banyak ibu langsung berpikir, “Jangan-jangan ASI aku kurang?”

Padahal, belum tentu. Bisa jadi si Kecil sedang memasuki fase leap, yaitu masa ketika otak bayi berkembang sangat pesat.

Di fase ini, bayi biasanya:
👶 Lebih sering ingin menyusu.
🫂 Maunya digendong terus.
🥺 Lebih mudah rewel dan menangis.
💤 Tidurnya jadi berubah.

Semua itu bisa menjadi respons yang normal karena bayi sedang belajar banyak hal baru dan mencari rasa aman dari Mommy.

Yang bisa Mommy lakukan:
🤱 Susui sesuai kebutuhan bayi, jangan batasi durasi maupun frekuensinya.
🫂 Perbanyak skin-to-skin untuk membantu bayi lebih tenang.
🤍 Respon tangisan si Kecil, karena bayi belum mampu menenangkan dirinya sendiri.
🌙 Kurangi stimulasi berlebihan dengan membawa bayi ke tempat yang lebih tenang.
🎵 Ajak berinteraksi sesuai mood bayi, tanpa dipaksa saat ia terlihat lelah.

Ingat ya, Mommy. Fase leap hanya sementara. Setelah melewatinya, sering kali si Kecil akan menunjukkan kemampuan baru sebagai bagian dari proses tumbuh kembangnya. 🌱✨

📌 Save postingan ini sebagai pengingat saat si Kecil sedang berada di fase leap, lalu share ke Mommy lain yang mungkin sedang overthinking karena bayinya tiba-tiba jadi lebih rewel. 🤍

Mental Anak: Orang Tua Normal vs Orang Tua NPD

Mental anak terbentuk dari cara orang tua memperlakukan, merespons emosi, dan berkomunikasi setiap hari. Ini yang jadi dasar kesehatan mental sampai dewasa.

Orang tua yang sehat menciptakan rasa aman, menghargai emosi anak, dan mendukung perkembangan anak. Sebaliknya, pola asuh yang tidak sehat bisa meninggalkan luka batin jangka panjang.

Catatan: NPD (Narcissistic Personality Disorder) adalah gangguan kepribadian yang hanya bisa didiagnosis profesional. Ini hanya perbandingan pola asuh, bukan diagnosis.

Perbedaan Orang Tua Normal dan Orang Tua NPD

1. Rasa Aman

Orang tua normal: anak merasa aman dan diterima meski salah.
Pola NPD: anak takut ditolak jika tidak memenuhi harapan.

2. Harga Diri

Orang tua normal: menghargai usaha anak.
Pola NPD: anak dihargai hanya saat membanggakan orang tua.

3. Kepercayaan Diri

Orang tua normal: anak didorong belajar dan mencoba.
Pola NPD: anak dikontrol atau diragukan terus.

4. Emosi

Orang tua normal: emosi anak divalidasi.
Pola NPD: emosi anak diabaikan atau disalahkan.

5. Hubungan Sosial

Orang tua normal: ajarkan empati dan komunikasi sehat.
Pola NPD: anak bisa belajar hubungan yang tidak sehat.

6. Dampak

Pola sehat → mental stabil & percaya diri.
Pola tidak sehat → cemas, rendah diri, sulit percaya orang.

Kesimpulan

Mental anak terbentuk dari lingkungan. Orang tua tidak harus sempurna, tapi perlu hadir dengan kasih sayang, komunikasi sehat, dan menghargai emosi anak agar anak tumbuh kuat secara mental.

Hadiah terindah untuk anak bukan mainan mahal.

Hadiah terindah adalah melihat ayah dan ibunya saling menyayangi, saling menghargai, dan membuat rumah terasa aman untuk ditinggali.

Karena yang paling membentuk masa depan anak bukan apa yang dibelikan orang tuanya, tetapi hubungan yang mereka lihat setiap hari di rumah.

Anak mungkin belum bisa menjelaskan perasaannya dengan kata-kata. Tapi tubuh dan ekspresinya sering kasih sinyal kalau dia sudah tidak nyaman, lelah, malu, atau tertekan 🥺

Hal-hal yang terlihat “sepele” di depan umum ternyata bisa membekas di hati anak lebih lama dari yang kita kira.

Seperti dipaksa tampil, dibandingkan, ditertawakan, atau dibahas kekurangannya di depan orang lain.

Yang sering orang dewasa anggap bercanda…
bisa jadi membuat anak merasa:
• tidak didengar
• tidak aman, minder
• malu menjadi dirinya sendiri
• takut mencoba lagi

Bukan berarti anak tidak boleh diarahkan atau diajarkan ya, Moms. Tapi cara menyampaikannya juga penting.

Anak lebih butuh:
✨ dipahami daripada dipermalukan
✨ didampingi daripada dipaksa
✨ diterima daripada dibandingkan

Karena rasa percaya diri anak tumbuh dari bagaimana orang terdekat memperlakukannya setiap hari.

Menurut Parents, poin mana yang paling sering tanpa sadar dilakukan orang dewasa ke anak? 👇

Tersedak susu atau gumoh yang berujung sulit bernapas bisa terjadi kapan saja. Karena itu, orang tua perlu tahu langkah pertolongan pertama yang benar dan aman.

👶 Apa yang Harus Dilakukan?
1️⃣ Tetap tenang. Panik justru membuat penanganan tidak optimal.
2️⃣ Posisikan bayi miring agar susu keluar dan tidak kembali masuk ke saluran napas.
3️⃣ Tepuk punggung bayi secara lembut dengan posisi kepala lebih rendah dari badan (back blow).
4️⃣ Perhatikan napas bayi. Jika sudah kembali teratur, gendong tegak beberapa menit.
5️⃣ Hindari memberikan minum segera setelah tersedak, beri waktu bayi tenang dulu.

❗ Waspadai tanda bahaya: bayi tampak sangat pucat, sulit bernapas, atau tidak menangis—segera bawa ke fasilitas kesehatan.

💙 Dengan mengetahui cara sederhana ini, orang tua bisa mencegah situasi kecil berubah menjadi gawat. Karena keselamatan si kecil selalu menjadi prioritas.

Kadang, pertanyaan unik dari anak bisa muncul puluhan kali sehari.

Tapi tahu nggak, itulah justru tanda fitrah anak sedang tumbuh sehat. 

👉 Dalam psikologi perkembangan, anak usia 2–7 tahun sedang ada di tahap pra-operasional.

Di tahap ini, anak belum bisa berpikir logis seperti orang dewasa. Mereka memahami dunia lewat apa yang terlihat dan dirasakan.

Karena itu, mereka sering bertanya “kenapa ini begitu?” bukan untuk membantah, tapi untuk memahami.

👉 Saat memasuki usia 7–11 tahun (tahap operasional konkret),

anak mulai belajar berpikir logis, tapi hanya untuk hal-hal yang nyata dan konkret.

Itulah sebabnya, penjelasan abstrak seperti “karena Allah tidak suka”

perlu dijembatani dengan cerita, perumpamaan, atau contoh yang mudah dicerna.

Jadi, ketika anak bertanya atau terlihat “membantah,” sebenarnya mereka sedang berusaha menyusun logika dan makna di kepalanya.

⁉️ Kalau setiap “kenapa” hanya dijawab dengan “karena Mama bilang begitu,”

perlahan anak akan berhenti bertanya.

Bukan karena mereka sudah paham, tapi karena merasa pertanyaannya tidak dihargai. 💔

Dalam Islam, berpikir dan bertanya adalah bagian dari fitrah manusia, bahkan sejak kecil.

Maka tugas kita bukan sekadar membuat anak nurut, tapi menuntun mereka mengenal “kenapa” di balik setiap kebaikan, agar ketaatan tumbuh bukan dari takut… tapi dari iman. 💜

This age can feel tricky right?! Some of these are just developmental stages you have to get through, but Here are some tips to help you survive 

-feeling stuck at home. At this age, they just want to be on the move. When out and about, switch up the scenery. Walk the stroller around to look at things. Bring a blanket with you to lay down on the grass so they can crawl around. And keep outings that you know will be frustrating short. Lower your expectations. If you get a 20 min coffee date in, take it as a win. It can also help to bring a new toy or a snack cup filled with snacks to keep them entertained. 

-saying dada - ugh. Why is that easier?! 🫠🤣 unfortunately this one just takes modeling, practice, and time. Just keep doing what you do and your moment will come! And it will be so worth the wait 💜

-naps - super common at this age to go through a random period of your baby taking forever to fall asleep for naps or skipping a nap altogether. So often parents assume their baby must just be ready for one nap. But the 12 month sleep regression looks just like this. Before you drop a nap, keep your schedule the same for 2 weeks, even if your baby takes a long time to sleep or never goes to sleep. It should clear up. And if it doesn’t, it may be time for one nap. 

-the head toss- this one is tricky. Because they aren’t at the age where they are able to manage their emotions and outbursts. Best thing you can do is anticipate the head toss and catch it before it happens. Keep your reaction relatively chill and neutral. And do your best to keep them (and your face!) physically protected.

How you hold your baby doesn’t have to look the same all day.

When you’re sitting and relaxing with them, spend plenty of time with your baby facing toward you. Let them see your face, make eye contact, talk to them, smile, and give them that face-to-face interaction.

But when your baby is fussy, especially when you’re walking around, out of the house, or just trying to settle them, changing positions can make a big difference.

This variation can be really comfortable because they’re more supported and upright while still being close to you. Sometimes simply changing the way you’re carrying them is enough to help them calm down.

The goal isn’t one “perfect” way to hold your baby. Mix it up based on what you’re doing, what your baby needs, and how they seem most comfortable.

Here’s what most parents don’t realise: if you’re flying with a baby under 2, they usually fly as a lap infant—but you can sometimes get them a seat for free… if you know what to do.

➡️ Take your car seat all the way to the gate
If the flight isn’t full, many airlines will let you use an empty seat for your baby’s car seat at no extra charge. You just have to ask at the gate because they won’t offer it unless you do.

💺 Make sure your car seat is FAA-approved (check the sticker before flying)
💡 My top recommendation is the Doona—because it’s a car seat with built-in wheels. You can roll your baby through the airport without lugging a separate pushchair

🕒 Think about how long your flight is
✈️ Short haul (<2 hours)? Honestly, probably not worth the faff. Just check the car seat at check-in (or take it to the gate if it’s a Doona and you’ll get to use it as a stroller straight off the flight)
🌙 Long haul? Absolutely worth it for everyone’s comfort and sleep

🛏️ Try to book overnight flights for long hauls—your baby is much more likely to sleep
👶🏼 Always bring a baby carrier onboard just in case the flight is full and you don’t get that extra seat. Wearing your baby makes everything easier—naps, turbulence, airport sprints… all of it 😅

🔹Temperature - keep it comfortable, you don’t want it too cold that it will shock them & obviously not too hot that it could cause a burn

🔹 Respond to their cues - *most* babies will be mesmerized by this sensory experience, but if you’re baby is already in an overstimulated state then they may not be a fan

🔹Try a modified version - if the actual running water seems to be too much for them, try filling a cup & pouring it slowly for a more gentle approach

❓Why does it work?

👉It’s an explosion for the senses

💥Watching the moving water

💥Feeling the water on their skin & some fun splashes too

💥 Listening to the running water is soothing because it’s very similar to the sound of blood flowing when they were cozy inside mama

🤩As they get older, it’s also a great way for them to learn cause & effect when you turn the water on & off

✨You don’t have to wait for your baby to be fussy to try this, it’s also just a fun activity to stimulate their brain during a wake window

🎉This hack will serve you well even into the toddler years when your little one needs to reset after a big feelings meltdown (as they get older, they’ll want to make their own splashes with their hands so be prepared for the mess😅)

Siapa nih yang masih reflek ngegas pas anak mukul? ✋

Menurut AAP dan IDAI, reaksi kita adalah contoh utama yang diingat anak. 

Hindari merespons dengan kekerasan, bentakan, hukuman, atau pembiaran, karena justru bisa membuat anak makin agresif dan menganggap teriak adalah cara sah menyelesaikan masalah.

Ini respon yang sebaiknya Bunbebs ambil menurut IDAI:

1. Tarik Napas: Jeda sejenak untuk menstabilkan emosi.
2. Pegang tangannya dan katakan dengan tegas tapi datar, “Ibu/Ayah tidak izinkan kamu memukul.”
3. Validasi Emosi: Katakan, “Kamu lagi kesal ya? Boleh bilang ‘kesal’, tapi tidak boleh pukul.”
4. Ajarkan Alternatif: Salurkan emosi ke hal aman (meremas bantal/kata-kata).
5. Evaluasi Nanti: Ajak ngobrol setelah anak tenang.

Parents — one second can change everything.
Children don’t understand danger, consequences, or outcomes yet. Their brain is still under construction — especially the prefrontal cortex, which is responsible for judgment, impulse control, and risk assessment🛠️

Between ages 0–7, children operate primarily from curiosity, imitation, and sensory exploration. They learn by touching, climbing, testing, and experiencing — not by forecasting harm.

So when they do something risky, it’s not “misbehavior”… it’s development.

That’s why supervision is not control — it’s protection.

As parents, our role is to be the nervous system that scans for risk when theirs cannot. It’s not about perfection, it’s about presence.

Micro Shifts for Conscious Parenting:
• Be attentive during active play (not just physically nearby)
• Reduce phone-based distraction during high-risk environments
• Redirect gently instead of shaming or yelling
• Model safety instead of only warning about it
• Child-proof spaces to reduce preventable accidents

Remember:
Children explore the world without the ability to predict consequences.
Parents provide the safety they cannot yet create for themselves🛠️❤️

14-17 hours a day in short broken stretches

No tub bath until the umbilical cord falls off

Quick and simple. Your baby isn't dirty 😂

Keep it dry. Keep it clean. Leave it alone

These are a few things I saved while I was pregnant that ended up being so helpful once we were actually home with him.

There is so much to remember in those first few weeks, and when you’re beyond exhausted, the last thing you want to do is try to remember how long breast milk can sit out, what wake window they should be in, how to dress them for sleep, or how much tummy time they need.

A few of the ones I kept going back to:

Feeding

* Most newborns are eating every 2–3 hours, but they can also cluster feed and want to eat as often as every hour for a stretch
* Amounts change pretty quickly those first few weeks
* Breast milk: 4 hours out, 4 days in the fridge, 6 months in the freezer
* One of the reasons we switched to bottles was because it was really helpful for us to be able to see exactly how much he was getting, especially when we were focused on getting his weight back up

Wake windows

* 0–2 months: around 45–60 minutes
* 2–3 months: around 60–90 minutes
* We’re a little over a month in and we’re still not trying to have him on any kind of routine at all, but it’s been really helpful just knowing roughly how long babies are actually awake between naps and how much they sleep at this age

Tummy time

* You can start tummy time basically as soon as you get home, even if it’s just 2–3 minutes a day at first
* Before his umbilical cord fell off, we mostly did tummy time on our chest instead of putting him flat on his belly
* Once the cord was off and healed, we started doing more little sessions on the floor throughout the day

Sleep

* Living in South Florida, I was SO worried about him getting overheated, so the room temperature + TOG charts were honestly some of the ones I looked at the most
* They made it so much easier to know what to dress him in depending on how warm the room was instead of constantly second guessing if he was too hot

Baby cues

* Rooting or sucking hands can mean hungry
* Yawning or looking away can mean tired
* Pulling legs up can mean gas
* Wide eyes and a calm body usually means they’re ready to hang out

Start from day one.

Let dad, grandma, a trusted person
put baby to sleep early.
Wait too long and only mom works.
Every. Single. Time.

Start blackout curtains from birth.
Light tells baby’s brain it’s daytime.
Their circadian rhythm is still forming —
you shape it now or fight it later.

Crib, bassinet, pack n play —
rotate early.
A baby who only sleeps in one place

Not tummy time. Just floor time.
On their back. Looking up.
Start from week one.
Builds tolerance for being put down
better than anything else.

✨👇🏼 Small changes but BIG results

⭐️ Offer feedings every 2-3 hours during the day!! We want baby to get in most of their calories during the daytime, so they don’t have to eat throughout the night and make up for any missed calories. We also want to avoid “snacking” throughout the day and aim for FULL feedings.

⭐️ Follow Eat, Play, Sleep. We want to avoid the feeding to sleep association because that is one of the hardest to break! Try to offer their feeding when your baby first wakes up to separate the two. This also helps baby to be more awake during the feeding, which will help ensure a full feeding vs baby falling asleep halfway through, and then waking after a short nap because they’re hungry again.

⭐️Follow wake windows! 30-90 minutes is normal for a newborn. They will be shorter the younger your baby is, and closer to the 90 minute mark as your baby nears 3 months. 

⭐️ Use positive sleep associations…aka swaddling and white noise!!

⭐️ Expose baby to a lot of natural light in the daytime! This will help develop babies’ internal clocks and natural circadian rhythm. 
 
⭐️ Create a bedtime routine that you follow in the same order EVERY. SINGLE. NIGHT. You can do this same routine before naps or a simplified version. Ex. Bath, diaper, pajamas, feeding, book, swaddle, sleep. 

If you can implement these, you will have laid a VERY strong foundation to get your baby sleeping LONG stretches at night 😍👏🏼

Some afternoons, the rain is the first thing I’ve listened to all day that doesn’t need an answer. It’s only when I step outside with my 2 year old that I realise I’ve been clenching my jaw since lunch.

In one experiment, researchers gave 40 adults a stressful maths task, then used sensors on their fingers to track how their bodies settled. In the four minutes afterwards, that physical stress signal was lower when they listened to birdsong and water than when they heard loud traffic. 

I think about what she gets to feel out here, too. The bounce beneath her feet. The weight of the umbrella in her hands. The rain making a sound she can stop and listen to for as long as she likes.

Sometimes I think I’m taking her outside to help her settle. Then I catch myself standing there in the rain, hoping she’ll want to stay out a little longer. 🤎

Confidence isn’t built by repeatedly telling children they’re amazing. 💛 It’s built when children have experiences that teach them, “I can do this.”

Two powerful ways we can help:

💪 1. Build competence, not just confidence.
Let them do the things they’re capable of doing — even when it would be faster or easier to do it ourselves. Cooking something simple, caring for a pet, packing their bag, helping with laundry, solving a problem, or mastering a new skill all give children evidence of their capability.

Praise can feel good, but competence gives children something to believe about themselves.

🧠 2. Help them learn to trust themselves.
Talk about what they notice, what they feel, and what their instincts are telling them. When children become more aware of their internal experience, they begin developing a sense of: “I know myself. I can listen to myself. I can trust myself.”

We can’t give our children confidence simply by telling them they’re confident.

We help them build it through experience. 🌱

Sometimes, “How was school?” is just too easy to answer with a simple “fine.” ❤️‍🩹

Kids don’t always know how to explain what happened during their day, especially when something is embarrassing, confusing, upsetting, or even surprisingly wonderful. Sometimes they need a question that gives them a little more room to talk. 🥹💭

Try asking things like:
✨ What made you laugh today?
🍎 Who did you sit with at lunch?
🏃‍♂️ What was the hardest part of today?
💡 Did anything surprise you?

A simple question can open the door to a much bigger conversation. One answer can lead to stories about friendships, worries, funny moments, school struggles, confidence, kindness, and things they may never have thought to mention on their own. 🫶

And sometimes, your child doesn’t need you to immediately fix the problem. They just need to know that you’re interested, that you’re listening, and that their little everyday experiences matter to you. ❤️

Those small conversations in the car, at dinner, before bed, or while walking home can become the moments they remember most. 🌱👨‍👩‍👦

Ask less for a report. Ask more for a story. Listen without rushing to solve. ❤️

Because behind a one-word “fine” might be a whole story waiting to come out. 🥰✨

Hello, everyone! I felt the need to leave a comment as this has picked up a lot of hate, When that was never my intention. I also don't have enough hours in my day to reply individually to you all, but I wanted to address some of the concerns here. This video isn't about making anyone feel guilty or ashamed. As parents, caregivers, and practitioners, we are all doing our best with what we know. This is simply a reminder of the important role we play in shaping children's emotional well-being through our words, actions, and presence. That said, parenting is complex, and every child is unique. Mental health is influenced by many factors, including genetics, life experiences, and individual neurodevelopment. Even if we do everything in our power as parents, some children are neurologically wired to experience the world differently, and challenges can arise regardless of how intentional we are. Many of us are also working through patterns from our own childhoods while trying to parent differently. That in itself is an incredible step, recognising what we want to change and making the effort to break cycles for the next generation. This isn't about blame - it's about awareness. It's about recognising our influence while also giving ourselves grace, knowing that perfection isn't the goal. What truly matters is showing up with love, intention, and the willingness to grow alongside our children!
